clue.text: Christmas spruce hiding one little girl (six)

indicators.note: the smart-looking word encloses the pieces that follow, as if keeping them out of sight

parts.note: spruce means smart and neat, natty
one is the Roman numeral I
Vi is a little girl's name, short for Violet, and VI is also six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A tidy Christmas tree with a small six-year-old girl tucked away behind it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spruce' looks like the Christmas tree but means smart. The bracketed 'six' confirms VI.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nativity is the birth of Jesus, the event Christmas celebrates.

clue.text: Requirement with second half of tale — one mustn't lose the thread

parts.note: a need is a requirement

indicators.note: the last two of the four letters of the story word

explanation.surface: A storyteller warned not to lose the plot halfway through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lose the thread' sounds like losing a story's plot, but it is the cotton in an eye.
explanation.definitionFit: A sewing tool would be useless if the cotton slipped out of its eye.

clue.text: Person dumping waste who may help 29

definitions.meaning: a diner who leaves extra money for the server at 29

explanation.surface: A rubbish collector who also lends a hand to the restaurant staff.
explanation.definitionFit: Tipping is both dumping rubbish and leaving a gratuity for a server.

clue.text: Extremely short opening for drink

indicators.note: short means cut off at the end

parts.note: very means extremely
the mouth is an opening

explanation.surface: A very brief introduction to a drinking session.
explanation.definitionFit: Vermouth is a fortified wine flavoured with herbs, drunk as an aperitif.

clue.text: Part of forest re-examined — something growing therein?

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Taking a second look at the woods.
explanation.definitionFit: A forest is full of these woody plants, so one grows within it.

clue.text: Animals in police cars

definitions.meaning: British police patrol cars were once called panda cars after their colour scheme

explanation.surface: Zoo creatures riding in squad cars.
explanation.definitionFit: Panda cars is old British slang for small police patrol cars; the giant panda is a bear.

clue.text: What's entertained us — dame cavorting

indicators.note: cavorting means leaping about, so the letters jump into a new order

explanation.surface: A pantomime dame prancing about to keep the audience happy.
explanation.walkthrough: A pantomime dame is the man-in-a-frock comic role in British Christmas pantomime.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has been diverted or made to smile has been entertained.

clue.text: Party people in charitable activity

parts.note: a do is a party
a nation is a people

explanation.surface: A political party's members out doing good works.
explanation.definitionFit: A gift to charity is a charitable act.

clue.text: Sirs here supply preprandial tipples?

indicators.note: read as supple-y, in a flexible way, so the letters bend into a new order

explanation.surface: Gentlemen being served drinks before dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' looks like a verb meaning provide, but it is the adverb from supple.
explanation.definitionFit: Fortified Spanish wines are classic aperitifs, taken before a meal.

clue.text: No more beer provided by business person

parts.note: ex means former, no longer the case
porter is a dark beer

explanation.surface: A trader whose supply of ale has run dry.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who sells goods abroad is a kind of businessperson.

clue.text: Fruit one of five children brought to church

parts.note: a quin is one of quintuplets, five born together
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A quintuplet taken along to church with some fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The quince is a hard, pear-shaped fruit used for jelly.

clue.text: Cleric has played lyre in merry-making

parts.note: Rev, short for Reverend, is a cleric

indicators.note: played suggests the letters are worked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A vicar strumming a harp-like instrument at a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Lively, noisy celebration is the same as merry-making.

clue.text: Dreadful woe — I'll hide away

indicators.note: something dreadful is in a terrible state, so these letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone so miserable they plan to go into hiding.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep out of sight and avoid notice is a common idiom for hiding away.

clue.text: Maybe watch moth consuming material?

indicators.note: the surface moth consumes material, so the eater word follows the cloth word as a material-eater

parts.note: rep is a ribbed fabric
a clothes moth is something that eats fabric, an eater

explanation.surface: A clothes moth munching its way through fabric, perhaps a watch strap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' marks a repeater as an example of a watch: one that chimes the time on demand.
explanation.definitionFit: A repeater is a watch or clock that strikes the last hour or quarter when a button is pressed.

clue.text: Peter's quaking outside front of castle — there's something spooky

indicators.note: the shaken letters sit outside the single letter
quaking means shaking, so the letters are shaken up
the first letter of the building word

explanation.surface: Peter trembling outside a castle with a ghost about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quaking' turns PETERS into SPETRE, which goes 'outside' C.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectre is a ghost, something eerie.

clue.text: Man remembered on Boxing Day taking walk with female

parts.note: a step is a single pace of walking
a hen is a female bird

explanation.surface: Someone out for a Boxing Day stroll with a woman friend.
explanation.walkthrough: Boxing Day, 26 December, is a British holiday that is also St Stephen's feast day.
explanation.definitionFit: The first Christian martyr's saint's day falls on 26 December, Boxing Day.

clue.text: Almost 12? Sleep

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a dozen is twelve

explanation.surface: Nearly midnight, time for bed.
explanation.walkthrough: '12' looks like a time of day but is a number of things.
explanation.definitionFit: To nap lightly is a synonym for sleeping briefly.

clue.text: English doctor hurried to be given a welcome

parts.note: MB is a Bachelor of Medicine
raced means hurried

explanation.surface: A GP rushing to be greeted on arrival.
explanation.definitionFit: To be hugged or received warmly is to be welcomed.

clue.text: Biscuits? They're exceptionally good

definitions.meaning: thin dry savoury biscuits, often eaten with cheese
a cracker is slang for an excellent thing

explanation.surface: Praising the biscuits on the table.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark hints that Christmas crackers, too, are no biscuits.
explanation.definitionFit: Crisp savoury wafers share the name with informal praise for something superb.

clue.text: Home dull, nothing right? I may help blow up balloons

definitions.text: I may help blow up balloons

parts.note: in means at home
flat means dull
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A boring party at home, nothing quite right, until the pump comes out.
explanation.definitionFit: A pump that fills balloons with air makes them bigger.

clue.text: Girl to wed, having given heart away

indicators.note: the middle letter of the word is removed, a pun on falling in love

parts.note: to wed is to marry

explanation.surface: A young woman about to marry after losing her heart to someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A common female first name, here a girl given by example, fitting the Nativity theme.

clue.text: Decorator with fluid in recreation facility

parts.note: an icer decorates cakes with icing
ink is a writing fluid

explanation.surface: A painter carrying a tin of liquid into a leisure centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decorator' suggests a painter, but here it is someone who ices cakes.
explanation.definitionFit: A rink for skating is a sports and leisure venue.

clue.text: A bit of carol making one hostile

parts.note: a carol is sung in verses

explanation.surface: One stanza of a Christmas song turning someone grumpy.
explanation.definitionFit: Being opposed or strongly disinclined is close to hostility.

clue.text: Man to joke, having held record

indicators.note: the joking word contains the record

parts.note: to josh is to tease jokingly
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A fellow kidding around while holding a vinyl disc.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph is a man's name, fitting the Nativity theme.

clue.text: Being terribly sedate, gets leg pulled

definitions.note: a passive phrase, matching the past participle

indicators.note: terribly suggests a mess, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A stuffy, staid person mocked by friends for being so dull.
explanation.definitionFit: Having your leg pulled means being joked with or ribbed.

clue.text: Getting better sports ground finished before end of January

parts.note: a rec is a recreation ground
over means ended

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of the month's name

explanation.surface: A player recovering from injury, with the sports field done for the winter by late January.
explanation.definitionFit: Recovery is the process of healing and regaining health.

clue.text: Gangster, old-fashioned fellow in hidden part of room?

parts.note: Al Capone is the archetypal gangster
cove is dated British slang for a man

explanation.surface: A mobster and an old-style chap lurking in a secluded corner.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that a recess is only partly hidden.
explanation.definitionFit: A recess set back into a wall is somewhat out of the main view of a room.

clue.text: Wise man maybe in picture I brought out

indicators.note: the single letter is taken out of the picture word

parts.note: an image is a picture

explanation.surface: A Magus shown in a Nativity painting.
explanation.definitionFit: A magus, one of the three Wise Men, is a magician or learned sage.

clue.text: Encourages good health!

definitions.meaning: urges on with shouts of support
a toast said when raising glasses

explanation.surface: A rousing toast to everyone's wellbeing.
explanation.definitionFit: To shout support urges someone on; the same word is a drinking toast.

clue.text: Server tries to move round — was seen going outside

indicators.note: the three-letter past tense wraps around the other letters
the letters are shifted about into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone tries to circle the room but is spotted heading out the door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Server' could be a tennis player or a computer; here it is restaurant staff, linking to 2-down.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who serves food at tables in a restaurant is a server.

clue.text: Cupid's companion, one in a hurry

definitions.meaning: Cupid is one of Santa's reindeer

explanation.surface: A lover's sidekick racing off.
explanation.walkthrough: Cupid here is not the god of love but one of Santa's reindeer.
explanation.definitionFit: Santa's reindeer team includes Cupid; someone rushing is one who darts about.

clue.text: Explored something growing maybe, having crossed bridge

indicators.note: the planted word spans the other, sitting on both sides of it

parts.note: a seed is something that grows, given as an example
an arch is a bridging structure

explanation.surface: A traveller who crossed a bridge to see what was growing beyond.
explanation.definitionFit: To search an area is to explore it thoroughly.
